title: What are Methods?
description: Discover the power of functions and methods to organize code, avoid repetition, and create reusable blocks.

slides.title: From Spaghetti to Structure 🍝
slides.content:
# Why Methods?

Imagine you need to make a character jump in five different places. Without methods, you'd write the same jump code five times. If you later need to tweak the jump height, you'd have to change it everywhere.

A **method** (also called a function) is a **named block of code** that you write once and call whenever needed. It makes your code:
- **Reusable**
- **Easier to read**
- **Easier to maintain**

quizData.question: What is the main benefit of using methods?

options.text: To make the game run faster
To organize code and reuse it

quizData.explanation: Methods help structure code into reusable blocks.

slides.title: Method Syntax ✍️
slides.content:
# Building a Simple Method

A method declaration has:
- **Access modifier** (public/private)
- **Return type** (void if nothing is returned)
- **Name** (PascalCase)
- **Parentheses** (may contain parameters)
- **Body** inside braces

```csharp
void SayHello()
{
    Debug.Log("Hello!");
}
```

To use it, just call its name:
```csharp
SayHello();
```

quizData.question: What does 'void' mean in a method declaration?

options.text: The method does not return any value

slides.title: Why Not Just Put Everything in Update? 🤯
Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## The SRP (Single Responsibility Principle)

Each method should do exactly one thing. If you find a method doing two things (e.g., moving AND checking health), split it. Your future self will thank you.
